subject: Next steps: trial evaluation plan & credentialing
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Chen <matthew.chen@shopwave.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@shopwave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: trial evaluation plan & credentialing

Hi Matthew / Olivia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off the 30-day trial with clear success criteria and the right access in place. I want to make the technical onboarding as low-friction as possible so your engineers can start running real traffic and we can validate latency/cost and output quality against your prompts.

High-level success criteria (what ShopWave cares about):
- End-to-end latency under 120ms P95 for single-turn product-description prompts (avg prompt length ~120 tokens)
- Token cost <= $0.0025 per input+output token for the POC workload
- >90% NPS on a 20-case prompt sample for brand-voice alignment
- Integration stability (no more than 2 transient errors / 1k requests)

Proposed evaluation plan and timeline:
1) Week 1 (this week): credentials & access, sample prompt set ingestion, baseline test runs
2) Week 2: performance tuning (batching/quantization suggestions), KV cache demo, instrumentation setup
3) Week 3: run workload replay and quality evaluation, iterate prompts
4) Week 4: finalize conclusions & optional canary to 5% production traffic

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marcus will provision API credentials, set up a trial model instance, and provide an initial performance dashboard. Priyom will be point on security/compliance questions and SSO invites.
- ShopWave: Matthew will own the sample prompt set and test harness; Olivia will coordinate network/IP allowlist and SSO admin invite.

Access we need from you to start:
- SSO invite for 2 engineers (SAML/Okta) or a list of emails for invite (preferred)
- IP allowlist ranges for your test runner(s) (we will whitelist at redwood edge)
- If you prefer API key route for the first 48 hours, let us know which option and Marcus will issue a scoped key (read/write, 100k token cap)

Attachments I've included: trial-eval-template.xlsx (success criteria template), MAP-Redwood-ShopWave.docx (mutual action plan), and a short SSO invite checklist.

Next immediate asks: can you confirm the two engineer emails for SSO or indicate you want a temporary API key? Also paste the IP ranges you want us to whitelist. I’ll have Marcus block time tomorrow to issue creds and run the first smoke test.

Thanks —

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: trial-eval-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), MAP-Redwood-ShopWave.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), sso-invite-guidelines.pdf (application/pdf)

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear plan. Happy to proceed. A few clarifying items before we confirm the engineer list:

1) Data residency: For the test data we're sending (sample SKUs + product copy), do you store any of the prompt payload on disk outside our tenancy, or is it ephemeral only in the inference path? We need this for our security team.
2) Sample prompt set: I'll attach a first-pass CSV of 25 prompts. Can you confirm how you recommend we format multi-turn checks for the brand voice evaluation?
3) IP ranges: our infra team can provide ranges — see below.

Engineer emails for SSO invite (if you can send SAML invites, please):
- daniel.cho@shopwave.com
- sofia.gomez@shopwave.com

IP ranges to whitelist (source runner egress):
- 54.213.120.0/22
- 3.12.45.0/24

We prefer SSO invites but are okay accepting an API key temporarily while SSO gets configured — whichever is fastest. If you can provision a key with a 100k token cap and restrict to the model instance we plan to use, that works for the first 48–72h.

Thanks,

Hi Matthew —

Quick answers: we do not persist prompt payloads to longer-term storage by default for hosted trials; payloads are processed in-memory and cached in KV only when you enable prefix caching. For the POC I recommend leaving caching off unless you need token-cost savings.

Audit logs: default retention for trial instances is 30 days; we can extend to 90 days on request. For SOC2/contract addenda, we can share the standard security addendum; please let us know if legal needs a copy.

I’ll issue the SSO invite checklist to Olivia and send the SAML/Okta metadata by end of day. Marcus — once you’ve generated the scoped key, please add the HubSpot secure note with the key stub and I’ll follow our secure handoff process.

Priyom Das
Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: sso-invite-guidelines.pdf
